provenance: Paraphrased reference text. No verbatim reproduction from Eric Berne's original. Slices are teaching-note reformulations of Berne's argument for ChapterFlow orchestrator use.

slices.label: The Autonomy Triad
slices.keyClaim: Three qualities constitute autonomy: awareness (direct perception), spontaneity (choice from full ego-state range), intimacy (game-free directness). Not techniques. What remains when games fall away.
slices.chapterUse: Core claim. All three qualities receive full treatment in separate paragraphs.

slices.label: Context: Games as Adaptive Behavior
slices.section: PART III — BEYOND GAMES > Significance / Players / A Good Life
slices.keyClaim: Games are adaptive, not contemptible. Players lack access to something better. Goal is not to win games but to become able to stop. Intimacy (direct, ulterior-free contact) is the better thing.
slices.chapterUse: Background for P2 and P6. Grounds the honest-limit framing in the chapter.

slices.label: Hard-Depth Tension: Failure Modes of Each Quality
slices.keyClaim: Each quality has a failure mode: awareness collapses into observation-as-practice; spontaneity collapses into compulsive reaction; intimacy requires both parties to be simultaneously pattern-free, which is rare.
slices.chapterUse: Required for hard depth content variants. Also appears in P6 of canonical prose.

slices.label: Continuity Discipline: Ch10 Cast
slices.keyClaim: Assigned names: Solenne, Casimir, Valeria, Takeshi, Fenna, Galina, Coach Oduya, Ottavia, Anneli, Elio, Mikkel. All confirmed absent from Ch1–Ch9.
slices.chapterUse: Character assignment for all 6 examples and the 3 prose anchors.

slices.label: Threshold Question
slices.keyClaim: Naming a direction is not the same as promising arrival. The catalog chapters are useful to readers who will never fully leave the games in them. The triad is useful in the same way.
slices.chapterUse: Required for hard depth threshold-question resolution. Also P6 of canonical prose.
